topic: cross-thread topic identity and incremental continuity in work communication

gaps.description: Which evidence combinations actually establish or refute continuity of a concrete work matter across independent workplace messages, conversations, attachments, email, and Teams remains open. The corpus supports adjacent-domain signals but does not validate subject, customer/project names, conversation ancestry, referenced artifacts, commitments, or state compatibility as target-domain identity evidence.
gaps.suggested_search_query: ("work item identity" OR "work matter identity" OR "business event coreference") AND (email OR "workplace communication" OR enterprise) AND (cross-thread OR cross-document OR cross-source)

gaps.description: The application-specific decision policy remains open: the relative cost of false merges versus false splits, thresholds for attachment versus rejection, and exact semantics/calibration of CONTINUE, NEW, and UNCERTAIN must be determined from msgloom requirements and empirical evaluation. The reviewed literature does not establish that false merges should receive a higher explicit cost.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve through application requirements and empirical decision-policy evaluation: define the operational consequences and costs of false merges and false splits, specify CONTINUE/NEW/UNCERTAIN semantics, build a representative labeled validation set, sweep decision thresholds, measure precision/recall and cost-weighted error, and calibrate thresholds against the chosen product risk policy.

gaps.description: The msgloom correction and identity-state model remains open. Stable Topic IDs independent of generated labels or source thread IDs, versioned identity assessments, supersession links, immutable evidence lineage, and general MERGE/SPLIT correction are project-level engineering choices not established by this corpus. They require design-document review, implementation prototypes, invariants, and correction-focused tests.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve through architecture and implementation work: define stable Topic-ID and identity-version schemas, evidence-lineage and supersession models, MERGE/SPLIT correction operations, referential and history-preservation invariants, then validate them with prototypes, migration scenarios, correction replay tests, concurrency tests, and persistence benchmarks.

gaps.description: There is no direct production-domain evidence in this corpus for longitudinal work-matter identity across Outlook email and Microsoft Teams. News, Wikipedia, image-recognition, public-health linkage, knowledge-graph, and database-process results cannot establish production accuracy or representativeness for msgloom.
gaps.suggested_search_query: (enterprise OR workplace) AND (email OR "Microsoft Teams" OR chat) AND (cross-thread OR longitudinal OR cross-conversation) AND (topic identity OR task tracking OR case tracking OR event coreference)

gaps.description: How partial, subevent, evolving, or otherwise non-transitive relations should map onto work-matter continuity is unresolved. CDEC-WN shows that event relations can be non-transitive, but no reviewed paper defines the corresponding semantics for workplace Topics.
gaps.suggested_search_query: ("partial event identity" OR "subevent relation" OR "event evolution" OR "non-transitive coreference") AND (workflow OR task OR case OR workplace)

gaps.description: The best operational strategy for Phase 2 evidence seeking is unresolved. Retrieval-based event-coreference search is promising adjacent-domain evidence, but msgloom still needs engineering benchmarks for bounded historical retrieval, candidate generation, latency, and whether additional context changes identity decisions.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve with controlled benchmarks over representative msgloom data: compare candidate-generation and historical-retrieval strategies at fixed recall targets, vary retrieval windows and top-k bounds, measure latency and memory cost, record how often retrieved context changes the identity decision, and select an operating point that meets both accuracy and latency requirements.

gaps.description: Calibration under non-stationary workplace streams remains unresolved. Selective-classification guarantees assume calibration data representative of deployment, while cross-corpus coreference results show material distribution sensitivity.
gaps.suggested_search_query: ("selective classification" OR abstention OR "confidence calibration") AND ("distribution shift" OR nonstationary OR streaming OR "concept drift") AND (text OR coreference OR clustering)

convergence.next_round_topic: direct evidence for cross-thread workplace work-matter identity, including cross-document business event coreference, enterprise email/chat continuity, and partial or evolving event identity
